speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: NOBODY CROSSES THE GORGE WITHOUT A SPOTTER. I AM THE SPOTTER.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: The bridge stays up by order of the regime and Chancellor Clench. Only iron matters! IRON! Also hydration!

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: You want the crank? Get through me first. Ten reps. Of PAIN.
new_text: YOU WANT THE CRANK? EARN YOUR TURN - TEN REPS OF PAIN!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: ...Oh no. Was I yelling? I was yelling. Sorry. That was the pre-workout talking, and it talks a lot.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: Chancellor Clench locked Grandmaster Flex in the House of Gains. People whispered the old man never broke. I didn't whisper. I yelled. Sorry again.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: The bridge is yours, friend. Stretch before you cross. Hamstrings are friends, and friends don't let friends pull one.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: HA! The pump is still MINE!

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: Come back when you can lift, shrimp. The bridge stays UP. Like my standards.
new_text: COME BACK WHEN YOU CAN LIFT! THE BRIDGE STAYS UP - FINALLY, SOMETHING THAT HOLDS ITS FORM!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: TASTE IT. TASTE IT! The Special Sauce is in everything. My soup. My tea. My SOUL.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: The pantry is closed by order of the Grand Chef. The key stays on my apron. For the war effort!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: You want in? Beat me first. Yes, Chef! No, YOU, Chef!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: The simmer let go. The sauce let go. Plain bread. No sauce. I could weep. I am weeping.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own sauces. The real one ALWAYS tasted. Same face. Ask yourself who was wearing the apron.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: The Test Kitchen is at the far end of the Buffet, and it was never making casserole. Take a biscuit. Take two. Heroes need carbs.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: Under-seasoned. NEXT!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: Come back when you have learned to cook. The pantry door stays shut. Like my oven, mid-souffle.
new_text: The pantry door stays shut until you learn to cook. Consider this a closed-course meal.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: ...the green is hungry... the green is HUNGRY... nothing goes to waste...

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: The Rot keeps this path for the Rotheart. Turn back. Turn back. Turn... into compost.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: If you will not leave, the hungry green will keep you. Forever. Very nicely. Like mulch.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: Oh. Oh no. Did I thorn at you? I'm so sorry. The Rot speaks very softly, right up until it doesn't.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything else grew out from her.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: The path is clear. Go gently in there. And if you see a raccoon, say hi. They're very good boys.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: ...the green is patient... it has all the time in the world... and so does the garbage...

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: Come back when you are ready to rot. Or, you know, not rot. Either is fine.
new_text: ...come back... the green can wait... it has nowhere to leaf...
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: Halt. This checkpoint requires a permit. Permits are not issued. Please take a number.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: Your number is zero. It is always zero. Now serving: nobody.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: The authorization is valid. Policy says I must stop you. I have read all of the policy. Twice.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: ...I can hear my own thoughts again. I think I was Pending for a decade. Old habits die hard. Unlike me.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: {villain} did not corrupt us. He used our own rules: a perfectly valid transfer of authority, notarized and filed.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: The Hall of Final Approvals is at the top of the D.N.A. Go carefully. Or fill out a form. Ideally both.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: Application denied. Please reapply in ten to twelve centuries.
new_text: Application denied; reapply in ten to twelve centuries. This is our express service.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: Not yet, then. Take a number. It is still zero.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Halt. ...Or don't. I am not a gate. I am a merchant's assistant. Security Protocol One: assess the customer's gait. Your gait is adequate.
new_text: Security Protocol One: assess the customer's gait. Adequate - you may approach at your current level of walking.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Bertram Beetsworth. Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. Not the Regional Merchant. Say it with me. No? Fine. It matters to me.
new_text: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Everything on this rack is inventoried and oiled under Security Protocol Seven. Protocol Seven is need-to-know. You do not need to know.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Do not reach for the drawer. The drawer is not for you. The drawer has never been for anyone.
new_text: Do not reach for the drawer. Its contents are classified, and so is your interest in them.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Back again. Returning customers are the backbone of a healthy economy, and of my employee-of-the-month case file.
new_text: A return customer strengthens the economy and my employee-of-the-month case file. Please look satisfied for the record.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Fact: the beets came in early this year. The bear has been informed. We have an understanding. I do not ask why it is here.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: The stones here were stacked by hands that stopped moving a long time ago.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: Something under the cairn is still keeping count of its turns. It has been keeping count since before {villain} came.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: Touch it, and it will not stop counting until one of you does.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: The counting stops. For now.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: Whatever was keeping time down there has nothing left to spend it on.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: The stones are just stones again. Take what it was guarding.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: It is still counting.

speaker: The Restless Cairn
current_text: Come back when you have more turns to spare than it does.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Grandmaster Flex walked into the throne room in his prison rags, and the room forgot how to breathe.
new_text: You watch Grandmaster Flex enter the throne room in his prison rags. No one speaks.
writer_note: Leader reveal: present tense, concrete image, no punchline.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Ten years without iron had left him thin. He breathed in, slow and even, and it was the loudest thing in the room.
new_text: You hear him breathe in, slow and even. Ten years without iron have left him thin.
writer_note: Preserves frailty and breath; strength remains heart and mind.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The ruler of the House of Gains took one step back. In this house, that is a scream.
new_text: Before you, the ruler of the House of Gains takes one step back.
writer_note: Removes the scream comparison from the sincere reveal.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The chef's perfect smile slid off her face like glaze off a very bad cake.
new_text: You watch the chef's perfect smile slip away with her face.
writer_note: Removes cake joke from the unmasking; present-tense image.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Underneath, nothing: a shifting shadow in a spotless white coat, wearing the best reviews in the kingdom.
new_text: Beneath it, you see a shifting shadow in a spotless white coat.
writer_note: Preserves faceless form; removes review-score joke.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Behind it, the unfinished war machines waited. They had been simmering for a long time.
new_text: Behind the shadow, you see the unfinished war machines standing still.
writer_note: Preserves machinery without a simmering punchline.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The great DENIED stamp cracked, and for the first time in the Department's long afterlife, it did not come down.
new_text: You hear the great DENIED stamp crack. For the first time in the Department's long afterlife, it does not come down.
writer_note: Leader reveal played straight; present tense.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Forms rose like startled doves. A thousand clerks looked up from their desks and remembered they had eyes.
new_text: Forms rise around you. Across the Department, a thousand clerks look up from their desks.
writer_note: Keeps the release image without the eyes joke.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Somewhere, a very small pen stopped writing. Nobody filed a complaint.
new_text: Somewhere nearby, you hear a pen stop scratching.
writer_note: Concrete quiet image replaces the complaint punchline.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Rotheart split open, and light poured out as if it had been waiting all along.
new_text: You see light pour through the splitting Rotheart.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The purple vines withered. At the heart of the wound, the Archdruid knelt, free and breathing.
new_text: Before you, the purple vines wither. At the heart of the wound, the Archdruid kneels, free and breathing.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Wildflowers followed the light outward. The Dump has seen worse mornings, but not many better.
new_text: You watch wildflowers follow the light outward through the Dump.
writer_note: Removes the better-mornings aside; lets recovery land.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The mirrors cracked one by one, and for the first time in ten years {villain} saw himself in them.
new_text: You hear the mirrors crack one by one. For the first time in ten years, {villain} sees himself in them.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: No crown. No perfect smile. Only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.
new_text: Above the small kingdom, you see a tired man kneeling without his crown or his perfect smile.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Light poured in through the broken glass. It did not feel like winning. It felt like the end of a long, quiet lie.
new_text: You stand in the light pouring through the broken glass.
writer_note: Ends on a visible image rather than instructing the player how victory feels.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: In the Capital's square, the leaders of the four Paths clasped hands. Nobody tripped. Several people cried.
new_text: In the Capital's square, you watch the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Several people cry.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Four banners flew from the same pole. It was a little crowded, and no one minded.
new_text: Above you, four banners share one crowded pole.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: At the edge of the crowd, a hooded traveler smiled, with leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
new_text: At the crowd's edge, you see a hooded traveler smile, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Forgotten Cave

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A cold draft rises from the dark. It smells of old stone and older water. The stranger said the town is on the other side. Go in?

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Fragment %d of 4: %s

speaker: (check key)
current_text: E / click: continue

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Warmth

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You're pale. Sit, sit. Something came back to you, didn't it?

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Tell me. All of it, however small.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: Light. Four colors of it, warm as bathwater, spilling across a ceiling I can't quite see.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: A woman is humming. A tune with no words, rising and falling like breathing.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: A hand rests on my head. Gentle. Certain. It smells of lavender and woodsmoke.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: Then the light thins, like breath on glass, and I am back.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: ...A lullaby. That tune is from the old days. From the court. Few remember it, and fewer hum it.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Eat some pie. Don't ask me why my eyes are wet.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: And look at you. With a zone free, the corruption's grip on the land is slipping, and it is slipping off you with it.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You should be able to carry a second Path now. Go on, try it at the Deck Station.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: A Second Path Opens

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: With the first zone free, the corruption smothering your gift has weakened. Your decks may now use two Paths, and dual-Path cards can finally be played.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: Decks may now use two Paths.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: The Cells

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Another one. Don't hide it behind your teacup. Say it.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: White rooms. White light that never changes with the hour.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: Glass on every side, and faces behind it in white coats, taking notes.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: They never use my name. They call me 'the Subject.' They say 'again.'

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: Again. Again. Again.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: I wasn't lost. I was kept.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Glass, and coats, and 'again.' So that is where you have been.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You have earned the truth, so here is the first piece of it: I am not only a tortoise who bakes.
new_text: You have earned the truth. I have been keeping more from you than I should.
writer_note: Memory beat: replaces the baking joke with a plain admission.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: There is a resistance in this kingdom, and I am its contact in {town}. Wren leads it, from a hideout in the Capital.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I wasn't sure of you before. I am sure now. Mostly.
new_text: I wasn't sure I could trust you before. I am now.
writer_note: Removes the mostly wink from the captivity-memory aftermath.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: The Coup

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You're shaking. Sit. Slowly now.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: A throne room at night. Candles guttering, banners with four colors woven as one.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: A man in white and gold kneels before the king. Soft voice. Then he stands.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: Hands on my shoulders. Two people pushing me behind them, toward the dark.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: I know that man's face. I have always known it. {villain}.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: A man in white and gold, kneeling, and then standing. And a lab with glass on every side.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I know that glass, because I helped to blow it. I founded the study of the Paths, long ago, for the best of reasons.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: {villain} took my work and turned it into a cage. My best student kept the lab running for him. And I ran.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I have been hiding my face in pie dough ever since.
new_text: I have been hiding here ever since.
writer_note: No pie punchline over Maren's guilt.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: That is my secret. Now you hold it, the same as I hold yours.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: A Name

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: There is something in your face today. The look of someone who has been handed a key. Tell me.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: A boy of eleven, in a coat too fine for the cold. Someone calls across a courtyard: '{prince}!'

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: I turn. A woman's voice. A man's voice. The {royal_house} crest on every door: four signs in a ring.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: {prince_full}. The son of the king and queen. Presumed dead.

speaker: (narration/UI)
current_text: That is who I am.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: {prince}. {prince} {royal_house}. I met a boy once at court, hiding behind his mother's cloak, who asked me why tortoises carry their houses.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I told him, 'So we are never far from home.'

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: And I knew. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only. I knew the moment you walked out of it, and I was too frightened to say so.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Four signs in a ring. The same as on my stick. I have carried it for ten years and told nobody why.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: And my lab, my life's work, was used on that boy. Forgive me, if you ever can.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: There is nothing to forgive. You gave me a bed and pie when you thought I might be a spy.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: ...Then let us make the kingdom a home again, {prince}.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You have the look of someone who was told something he did not want to hear. {villain}?

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Sit. Tell me what he said.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: So he knew you from the first. He told you, and you came to me for the rest.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I knew too, dearie. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only. I knew, and I was too frightened to say it.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: So hear it from the one who held your hand at court: you are {prince_full}, and I am so sorry for what was done to you in my name.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Eat. Rest. Mind the questions you ask out loud, dearie. This town has ears.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: And stop staring at my stick. Four little carvings in a ring, older than you, and none of your business.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You are warmer than you were. Don't mistake me, dearie, I am still watching you. The watching is free.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: My pie recipe is pinned by the door, in my own hand. Round letters, careful loops. Copy it if you like. Smudge it and I will know.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Somebody in the square says you have a look of the old court about you. That is no prince, I told them. That is a damp young man with good posture.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: And if you meet Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in the kingdom. She'll argue. She'll be wrong.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I have told you the worst of me. The rest is easy, by comparison.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Go on. The next zone will not free itself, and I am far too slow to do it for you.
new_text: Go on, dearie, the next zone won't free itself. At my pace, we'd have to outlive the regime.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: {prince}. I keep wanting to curtsy. My knees have voted against it.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Go on: the kingdom is waiting, and so is the pie.
new_text: Go on, the kingdom is waiting. The pie has less patience.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: {prince}. {villain} let it slip to you, didn't he, that smug man. I had hoped to tell you myself.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Sit. When you are ready, the memories will come, and I will be here. With pie. Obviously.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Up and walking. Good. I am Elder Maren, dearie, and this is {town}, where the four Paths used to meet, and argue, and borrow each other's pans.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Then {villain} took the Paths, one by one, and set his rulers over them. Every road out of town has a gatekeeper now: a bridge, a barrier, a pantry door, a wall of thorns.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Beat a gatekeeper and its road opens. Buy cards from Sable, fix your deck at the Deck Station, and come back to me for pie. Not answers. Pie.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: The roads are waiting, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. One zone at a time.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You could still be anyone's spy. I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Still here, dearie? The roads won't walk themselves. Well. Some of them would, if {villain} let them.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: There's pie on the sill. Cooling. Which means no, not yet.
new_text: The pie on the sill is cooling, dearie. Unlike you, it knows when to wait.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: If you're looking for advice: eat something. If you're looking for more advice: eat something else.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I've told you everything you need for now. The rest you'll have to go and get yourself. That's the annoying part.
new_text: I've given you all the answers you need for now, dearie. Further questions require fieldwork.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Mind the fountain, dearie. People throw wishes in it. Most of them are mine.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Off you go. I'll be here. I'm always here. It's one of my better qualities.
new_text: Off you go, dearie; I'll be here. I'm dependable at a speed you can barely measure.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: One zone free. Hm. And the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started cheering at night. From the cellar. I am choosing not to ask.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Two zones free. Auntie Alembic has opened her shop on the square, the Alchemist's.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: She asks for your leftovers. From her, that is a compliment.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Three zones free. Only one Path left under {villain}'s thumb. I will not say what I'm feeling. I will say it is a lot of feelings.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: All four Paths are free. {kingdom} is whole again, or nearly. And up in his castle, {villain} is counting what he has left.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Rest. Then we finish this.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: {villain} is gone, and the Paths are shouting at each other in the street again. I have never been so glad to be annoyed.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: The Capital is open to everyone now, and your decks may mix any Paths you like. Go and see what you can make of it, dearie. Then come home and eat.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
current_text: ...Hm. Woken. For this. Another of the little scavengers, I suppose.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
current_text: ...No. Not that. You smell familiar. Like old stone, and cold nights, in a house I used to keep.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
current_text: The house does not open for just anyone. ...Show me.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
current_text: ...Yes. The old walls do not lie. The spring at the end ran once. You would not remember.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
current_text: Go. The house is yours to leave. Someone is waiting at the far end with a kettle on.
